title: From source contracts to verification of existing JS/TS
status: A, B, C, D, F, E, J, H and G are integrated. P is in implementation; the stateful foundation has a selected design with mandatory corrections. K is in independent design and numeric review. The local-result upstream pilot passed implementation checks and is in independent review. No remaining roadmap node is claimed complete.
edgeMeaning: All prerequisites apply. The implemented first subsets of H and G are merged. P and T can proceed independently; K, R and S now have their original prerequisites. The stateful foundation is being designed together. Transitively redundant edges are omitted.
assumptions: Properties and environment assumptions are supplied explicitly; this is not automatic proof of arbitrary JavaScript.
Each node is a work package, not an equal-duration task or one person.
The async extension can advance alongside pure-library work once its own prerequisites are ready.
No duration, cost or capacity estimates have been assigned.
Integrated status refers to the documented first-layer subsets. Readiness of downstream work does not mean those capabilities exist.

nodes.title: Current verifier
nodes.detail: Binary64 scalars, dense arrays and plain records, every contracts, same-file calls, named local imports, source hashes, JavaScript replay and dependency gating.
nodes.doneWhen: Current baseline exists; 84 verifier tests passed in the latest implementation run.

nodes.title: Scalar state & control flow
nodes.detail: Model local let/var bindings, assignments, updates such as ++, early returns and control-flow joins. Preserve JavaScript evaluation order and binary64 semantics.
nodes.doneWhen: Local scalar state changes compile and replay faithfully, with unsupported effects rejected.
nodes.resultSummary: Local let/var scalar updates, expression effects and control-flow joins are integrated. Parameter writes, reference writes and loops remain unsupported.

nodes.title: Proof scaling & backend API

nodes.doneWhen: One costly obligation cannot erase unrelated useful results; backend uncertainty never becomes a proof.
nodes.resultSummary: Independent obligations, fair two-worker scheduling and explicit backend capabilities are integrated. Z3 remains the only backend.

nodes.title: Richer specifications
nodes.detail: Add the specification tools demanded by real proofs: pre-state values, reusable pure specifications and lemmas, and exact mathematical reasoning with explicit bridges to JavaScript numbers. Separate specification-only values from runtime operations.
nodes.doneWhen: Specs compose without unchecked axioms, and every numeric bridge states its finiteness and exactness obligations.
nodes.resultSummary: Entry snapshots with old(...), checked @spec definitions/lemmas and exact rational contracts are integrated. Mutable-heap old semantics remain unsupported.

nodes.title: Integrate & validate
nodes.detail: The five branches are combined. Compiler scopes, scalar bindings, exact specifications, independent proof obligations and corpus mutations work together. All 168 combined tests pass without weakening contracts, assertions or proof domains.
nodes.doneWhen: The branches work together, all combined checks pass without weaker contracts, assertions or proof bounds, and D's acceptance gap is closed. Only then count this batch as integrated.

nodes.title: Loops with induction
nodes.detail: Check invariant initialization and preservation at loop heads, then derive exit and early-return properties. Check a well-founded decreasing measure when termination is claimed. Use induction rather than bounded unrolling.
nodes.doneWhen: Read-only-array loops verify for every native length; bad invariants and non-decreasing termination measures fail.
nodes.resultSummary: Annotated for/while loops use checked initialization, preservation and unit rank decrease, with early returns, break/continue, optional scalars and unchanged-source replay. Nested loops and heap writes remain unsupported.

nodes.title: Heap, aliases & frames
nodes.detail: Model object/array identity, shared references and writes. Contracts describe pre-state values and permitted mutation footprints, so helper calls preserve facts outside their effects.
nodes.doneWhen: Proofs distinguish a fresh copy from an alias and remain sound when two arguments share storage.
nodes.resultSummary: Shared record/array identities, shallow-copy freshness, entry heaps, primitive stores and per-write mutation frames compose through checked helpers. The full suite passes 249/249 and four heap-specific verifier mutants are detected alongside the twelve existing mutants. Mutating loops, reference stores and stateful callbacks remain unsupported. Independent landing review repeated 249/249 and exercised 92 probes; merged in PR #6.

nodes.title: Higher-order contracts
nodes.detail: Give callbacks and closures checked parameter/result contracts, with explicit captured-value and effect assumptions. Begin with pure callbacks; stateful callbacks also require the heap model when used.
nodes.doneWhen: Selected generic/callback helpers compose through checked function contracts without treating arbitrary callbacks as trusted.
nodes.resultSummary: Pure total unary numeric predicates compose through checked callback admission, immutable primitive captures and named contracts. The unchanged Ramda eager findIndex verifies; two seeded bugs replay. Final suite passes 219/219 and all 12 verifier mutants are detected. Stateful callbacks remain unsupported. Independent landing review passed 219/219 and 29 adversarial probes; merged in PR #5.

nodes.title: Search proof pilot
nodes.detail: Pin Lodash strictIndexOf at c6e281b. Prove bounds, first match, absence and termination for dense numeric arrays and valid integer starts. Replay off-by-one and skipped-first-match mutants.
nodes.doneWhen: The unchanged helper verifies and a seeded implementation bug gives a replay-confirmed counterexample.
nodes.resultSummary: The unchanged Lodash strictIndexOf declaration verifies integer result, bounds, first match, absence and termination. Both seeded bugs produce replay-confirmed counterexamples. The final suite passes 199/199 tests; the raw export passes 261 native comparisons.

nodes.title: Broader library proofs
nodes.detail: Verify a selected corpus of unchanged library implementations, including helpers that mutate local storage or accept callbacks. Record contracts, assumptions, unsupported code and confirmed counterexamples.
nodes.doneWhen: Multiple realistic functions compose, seeded bugs are caught, and results survive contract/source changes honestly.

nodes.title: Project proof workflow
nodes.detail: Select proof targets, rerun affected functions in CI, shrink and replay witnesses, and report useful source-level failures. Any cached result includes source dependencies, contracts, semantic model, configuration and backend identity.
nodes.doneWhen: A dependency or verification-model change invalidates affected results; a reviewer can reproduce every reported bug or proof.

nodes.title: Pure JS/TS proofs & bugs
nodes.short: Useful proofs and real bug finding
nodes.detail: Take existing JS/TS in the supported subset, add explicit contracts and purity/environment assumptions, and produce useful property proofs or reproducible real bugs in substantial software. Unknown remains an honest outcome.
nodes.doneWhen: Independent real-code campaigns produce reproducible bug reports and maintained universal proofs, without rewriting the implementations.

nodes.title: Event & lifecycle semantics
nodes.detail: Model registering/removing listeners, callback identity, lifecycle ownership and legal state transitions. Callback writes use heap footprints rather than assumed purity.
nodes.doneWhen: Listener/disposal safety properties hold across arbitrary modeled event sequences, including stale events.

nodes.title: Async ordering model
nodes.detail: Model suspension, resumption, Promise outcomes, cancellation and relevant happens-before relations. Specify the supported event-loop scheduling abstraction and its environment assumptions.
nodes.doneWhen: Proofs account for allowed interleavings and detect a seeded stale-response or cancellation bug.

nodes.title: Environment contracts
nodes.detail: Specify external operations through nondeterministic outcomes and protocol contracts: success, failure, timing and response shape. Assumptions about servers and the browser remain visible rather than becoming implicit guarantees.
nodes.doneWhen: External behaviors and fairness assumptions are explicit, replayable and distinct from properties proved about application code.

nodes.title: Temporal verification
nodes.detail: Translate supported stateful source behavior into transition obligations. Check safety across event sequences and liveness under stated scheduling/fairness assumptions. Choose SMT, induction or model-checking backends by the property.
nodes.doneWhen: Source-linked state properties and counterexample traces are supported without a hidden event-count bound.

nodes.title: Stateful app pilots
nodes.detail: Pin representative applications or subsystems. Connect actual code, transition models, environment contracts and executable event traces; preserve known race/lifecycle failures as regressions.
nodes.doneWhen: A real lifecycle or async bug is reproduced from a source-linked trace, and the corrected code satisfies the stated property.

nodes.title: Existing JS/TS verification
nodes.detail: Human-assisted verification and bug finding for supported existing JS/TS, covering both algorithms and stateful async behavior under explicit assumptions. This does not promise decidable or automatic proof of every JavaScript program.
nodes.doneWhen: Real pure and stateful software has maintained proofs and reproducible bugs, with supported semantics, dependencies and trust boundaries visible.

edgeDisplay: Transitively redundant edges omitted; reachability is unchanged. capabilityDeps retains the earlier capability inputs.
